name: PrestaShop
description: Your own PrestaShop shop: products and combinations, stock, orders with their status history, customers, addresses, carriers and categories, through the shop's Webservice API. Change an order's status, a product's price or a stock quantity.
instructions:
## PrestaShop
This connector talks to the **Webservice API** of a self-hosted PrestaShop shop (`<shop address>/api`). It asks for JSON on every call (`output_format=JSON`). Reading works on PrestaShop 1.7 and 8; the two update tools (`prestashop_update_product_price`, `prestashop_update_stock_quantity`) use `PATCH`, which the Webservice offers from **PrestaShop 8.0**.

## Setup
1. In the back office open **Advanced Parameters → Webservice** and set **Enable PrestaShop's webservice** to **Yes**. Save.
2. On the same page click **Add new webservice key**. Click **Generate** for a 32-character key, add a description, set **Status** to enabled.
3. Under **Permissions** tick, per resource, the methods the key may use. For everything this connector does: **GET** on `products`, `combinations`, `stock_availables`, `orders`, `order_states`, `order_histories`, `customers`, `addresses`, `carriers`, `categories`; **POST** on `order_histories` (change an order's status); **PATCH** on `products` and `stock_availables` (price and stock). A read-only key needs only the GET column. In multistore mode, also pick the shop(s) the key may reach.
4. Paste the shop address into `PRESTASHOP_URL` (the root, e.g. `https://shop.example.com`, or `https://example.com/shop` when the shop lives in a folder; no `/api`, no trailing slash) and the key into `PRESTASHOP_WEBSERVICE_KEY`.

The key travels as the username of HTTP Basic authentication with an empty password. Behind Apache with PHP as CGI/FastCGI, the `Authorization` header can be dropped before PrestaShop sees it (every call then answers 401): enable **CGI mode for PHP** on the Webservice page, or fix the server so it passes the header.

## Lists: display, filter, sort, limit
- **display**: without it, a list returns only ids. `full` returns every field; `[id,name,price]` returns the fields named. Customer tools always return a fixed set of fields that leaves out the password hash and secure key.
- **filters** (where offered): extra query parameters in PrestaShop syntax, joined with `&`, for fields the tool has no argument for, e.g. `filter[date_upd]=[2026-01-01,2026-12-31]` or `filter[ean13]=[4006381333931]`. Value syntax: `[a]` exact (case-insensitive), `[a|b]` one of, `[1,10]` range, `[ab]%` starts with, `%[ab]` ends with, `%[ab]%` contains. Filtering or sorting by a field the resource does not have is answered with HTTP 500 and error code 38, which lists the fields that can be used.
- **sort**: `[field_ASC]` or `[field1_DESC,field2_ASC]`.
- **limit**: `20` for the first 20 rows, `40,20` for 20 rows starting at offset 40. There is no total count; page until a call returns fewer rows than asked for. An empty result comes back as `[]`.
- Dates (`date_add`, `date_upd`) can be filtered and sorted; the order tool already sends the `date=1` switch PrestaShop needs for that.
- **language**: multilingual fields (product `name`, `description`, `link_rewrite`, category and order status `name`) come back as a list of `{id, value}` per language when the shop has several languages; pass a language id (`1`) to get plain text.

## Money and stock
- Product `price` is the base price **without tax**, in the shop's default currency. Order totals come in `total_paid_tax_incl` / `total_paid_tax_excl`, in the order's currency (`id_currency`, `conversion_rate`).
- Stock lives in `stock_availables`, one row per product and combination: `id_product_attribute` 0 is the product row, other rows are its combinations (sizes, colours). For a product with combinations, change the combination rows; the product row holds their total. A product with `depends_on_stock` 1 is managed by advanced stock management and its quantity cannot be set here.

## Order status
`prestashop_list_order_states` gives the shop's statuses (ids differ between shops). `prestashop_change_order_state` adds a row to the order's history, which is how PrestaShop changes `current_state` and runs what the status triggers (invoice, stock movements, and, with `send_email` 1, the status e-mail to the customer). PrestaShop changes the status before it sends the e-mail; if the shop cannot send it, the answer is *Unable to save resource* (code 46) although `current_state` has already changed. Check with `prestashop_get_order` before trying again.

## Rate limits
PrestaShop sets none; the shop's own server is the limit. Prefer `display=[…]` with the fields needed over `display=full` on long lists.

## Common errors
- **401** *Authentification key is not active* / *No permission for this authentication key*: wrong or disabled key, or the `Authorization` header is lost (see CGI mode above).
- **401 / 405** on one resource only: the key lacks that method for that resource; tick it under Permissions.
- **503** *The PrestaShop webservice is disabled*: switch the Webservice on (step 1).
- **404** on `/api`: the shop has no friendly URLs rewrite (`.htaccess`) for the API; regenerate it under **Shop Parameters → Traffic & SEO** (save with Friendly URL on).
- **405** on the update tools: the shop runs PrestaShop 1.7, whose Webservice has no `PATCH`.

PRESTASHOP_URL.label: Shop address
PRESTASHOP_URL.help: The https:// address of the shop's front office, including the folder if the shop lives in one. Without /api and without a trailing slash.
PRESTASHOP_URL.patternMessage: The https:// address of the shop root, without a trailing slash or /api.

PRESTASHOP_WEBSERVICE_KEY.label: Webservice key
PRESTASHOP_WEBSERVICE_KEY.help: Back office → Advanced Parameters → Webservice → Add new webservice key → Generate. Tick the GET permission for the resources to read, POST on order_histories and PATCH on products and stock_availables for the write tools.
PRESTASHOP_WEBSERVICE_KEY.patternMessage: A PrestaShop webservice key is 32 letters and digits.

verifyHints.401: PrestaShop refused the key. Check that it is enabled under Advanced Parameters → Webservice and has GET on products. If the key is right, the server may drop the Authorization header: enable CGI mode for PHP on the Webservice page.
verifyHints.404: No PrestaShop Webservice at this address. Check the shop address (root of the shop, without /api) and that friendly URLs are on, so /api is rewritten.
verifyHints.503: The PrestaShop Webservice is switched off. Enable it under Advanced Parameters → Webservice.

tools.name: prestashop_list_products
tools.description: List products of the shop, with filters on id, reference, name, active flag and default category. Without display only ids come back; display=full returns every field, [id,name,price,reference,active] only those. price is the base price without tax.

display.description: full, or a field list such as [id,name,reference,price,active,id_category_default,date_upd]. Omitted: ids only.

id.description: Product id, or several separated by | (e.g. 3|7|12).

active.description: 1 for enabled products, 0 for disabled ones.

filters.description: Further filters in PrestaShop syntax joined with &, e.g. filter[ean13]=[4006381333931] or filter[date_upd]=[2026-01-01,2026-12-31].

limit.description: 20 for the first 20 rows, or offset,count such as 40,20.

language.description: Language id: multilingual fields such as name come back as plain text in that language instead of a list per language.

tools.name: prestashop_get_product
tools.description: Get one product with all its fields: prices (base price without tax, wholesale price), reference and EANs, descriptions, active flag, and associations to categories, images, combinations, features and stock_availables rows.

language.description: Language id for plain-text multilingual fields.

tools.name: prestashop_list_combinations
tools.description: List the combinations (variants such as size and colour) of products: reference, EAN, price impact on the product price, weight impact, default flag and the attribute values (product_option_values) that make the combination.

product_id.description: Only the combinations of this product.

id.description: Combination id, or several separated by |.

tools.name: prestashop_list_stock_availables
tools.description: List stock rows: quantity per product and combination (id_product_attribute 0 is the product row), out-of-stock behaviour and whether advanced stock management drives the row (depends_on_stock). The row id is what prestashop_update_stock_quantity needs.

product_id.description: Only the rows of this product.

product_attribute_id.description: Only the row of this combination id (0 for the product row).

quantity_range.description: Quantity range min,max, e.g. -100,0 for products out of stock or oversold.

tools.name: prestashop_update_product_price
tools.description: Set a product's base price without tax, in the shop's default currency. Only the price changes; the other fields of the product stay as they are. Needs PrestaShop 8 or later and the PATCH permission on products. Returns the updated product.

price.description: New base price without tax, e.g. 24.5.

tools.name: prestashop_update_stock_quantity
tools.description: Set the quantity of one stock row (a product or one of its combinations) to an absolute number. Take the row id from prestashop_list_stock_availables. Needs PrestaShop 8 or later and the PATCH permission on stock_availables. Returns the updated row.

tools.name: prestashop_list_orders
tools.description: List orders, filtered by id, reference, customer, current status or a date range on date_add. Without display only ids come back; display=full returns totals, addresses, carrier, payment and order lines. current_state is an order status id from prestashop_list_order_states.

display.description: full, or a field list such as [id,reference,id_customer,current_state,total_paid_tax_incl,payment,date_add].

id.description: Order id, or several separated by |.

current_state.description: Order status id, or several separated by | (e.g. 2|3).

date_from.description: Orders placed on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS). Needs date_to as well.

date_to.description: Orders placed on or before this date. Needs date_from as well.

filters.description: Further filters in PrestaShop syntax joined with &, e.g. filter[id_carrier]=[2] or filter[valid]=[1].

tools.name: prestashop_get_order
tools.description: Get one order: customer, delivery and invoice address ids, carrier, payment method, current status, totals with and without tax, currency, and the order lines (product, combination, quantity, unit prices).

tools.name: prestashop_list_order_states
tools.description: List the shop's order statuses with id, name and flags: paid, shipped, delivery, invoice, whether the customer gets an e-mail (send_email) and the e-mail template. Ids differ between shops.

tools.name: prestashop_list_order_histories
tools.description: List the status history of orders: each row is one status change with the order id, the status id, the employee who made it (0 for the system) and its date.

order_id.description: Only the history of this order.

tools.name: prestashop_change_order_state
tools.description: Move an order to another status by adding a row to its history. PrestaShop then updates current_state and runs what the status triggers (invoice, stock movements). With send_email 1, the customer gets the status e-mail if the status has one. Returns the new history row.

send_email.description: 1 to send the customer the e-mail tied to the status. 0 or omitted: no e-mail.

tools.name: prestashop_list_customers
tools.description: List customer accounts with name, e-mail, company, group, language, newsletter and opt-in flags, guest flag, active flag, note and dates. The password hash and secure key are never returned.

id.description: Customer id, or several separated by |.

active.description: 1 for active accounts, 0 for disabled ones.

tools.name: prestashop_get_customer
tools.description: Get one customer account by id: name, e-mail, company, group, language, newsletter and opt-in flags, guest flag, active flag, note and dates. The password hash and secure key are never returned.

tools.name: prestashop_list_addresses
tools.description: List postal addresses with name, company, VAT number, street lines, postcode, city, country and state ids, phones and the customer they belong to. Orders point to them through id_address_delivery and id_address_invoice.

id.description: Address id, or several separated by | (e.g. the delivery and invoice address of an order).

customer_id.description: Only the addresses of this customer.

tools.name: prestashop_list_carriers
tools.description: List carriers with id, name, active and deleted flags, delivery delay text, tracking URL and limits. PrestaShop keeps the old version of an edited carrier as a deleted row with its own id, so older orders can point to a deleted carrier.

id.description: Carrier id, or several separated by |.

active.description: 1 for carriers offered at checkout, 0 for disabled ones.

deleted.description: 0 for current carriers, 1 for replaced or deleted ones.

language.description: Language id for the plain-text delay.

tools.name: prestashop_list_categories
tools.description: List product categories with id, name, parent id, depth in the tree, active flag and, with display=full, descriptions and associated products. The tree starts at Root (id 1) and Home (id 2).

display.description: full, or a field list such as [id,name,id_parent,level_depth,active]. Omitted: ids only.

id.description: Category id, or several separated by |.

parent_id.description: Only the direct children of this category.

active.description: 1 for visible categories, 0 for hidden ones.
